response.title: FY2027 Budget Request to Open a Sixth Site
response.dek: Staff want the board to approve a $1,610,000 FY2027 budget that adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library to bring down a growing waitlist.

stat.label: Proposed FY2027 budget, with a sixth site

sections.heading: The staff request
sections.body: Staff propose an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. The budget opens a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and adds two site coordinators. Staff think the new site would serve 180 more learners a year. They expect it to cut the waitlist in half.

sections.heading: Why more people need help
sections.body: Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in FY2026. The year before, it enrolled 936. At year end, 287 adults were waiting for a seat, mostly at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. They waited nine weeks on average.

sections.heading: What the money pays for now
sections.body: Operating expenses in FY2026 were $1,420,000. Program costs made up 81 percent of spending. Each learner cost $1,237. Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks moved up one or more reading levels. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential, more than in any year in Harborlight's history.

sections.heading: Where funding comes from
sections.body: In FY2026, foundation grants brought in $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000, and the city contract paid $295,000. The treasurer said reserves cover 3.2 months of operating expenses. The board's target is 4 months, so reserves fall short.

points.text: 287 adults waited nine weeks on average for a seat
A sixth site could serve 180 more learners each year
214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 hours in FY2026
Reserves are at 3.2 months, below the 4-month target

quote.text: I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring.
quote.who: A learner at the Riverside site

response.next: The board planned to vote on the FY2027 budget at its October 21 meeting.
